transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is that I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. It's... it's like, I'll be right in the middle of fixing a rendering bug at work—which, by the way, the new graphics engine they have us using is just a complete mess. I was actually telling my buddy Dave about it. Dave's this guy I met at a hackathon back in, what, 2018? Great guy, he actually makes these amazing artisanal hot sauces now, completely left the tech industry. I don't blame him, honestly. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Right, the code. So I'll be fixing this bug, and then I get a Slack ping, or I'll just notice a weird color pattern on my screen, or even just a siren going by outside, and boom. It just pulls me into a completely new idea before I can even finish typing the line of code. Speaking of sirens, did you know they changed the pitch of the ambulances around here? It's a whole Doppler effect thing, I went down this massive rabbit hole reading about it the other night... but yeah, that's why I'm here. I just can't stick to one thought.
Do you find yourself taking on a lot of projects or activities at once, or feeling more energetic or restless than usual?

Oh, absolutely. Energetic doesn't even begin to cover it. I've got so many things going on right now. I've been emailing all these art curators, pitching community leaders, and completely rewriting the backend for this massive new system I'm building. Which, by the way, rewriting a backend from scratch is wild. We used to use this ancient PHP stack at my first job right after I got my degree—my boss there, Greg, he actually still used a Blackberry. In like, 2015! He swore by the physical keyboard. I kind of get it, the tactile feedback is nice. I actually looked into buying a custom mechanical keyboard recently, the ones with the Cherry MX Blue switches? They're so loud though, my downstairs neighbor would probably complain. She complains about everything, even when I'm just watering my plants on the balcony. She has this tiny little yappy dog that never stops barking, but *I'm* the loud one. 

But wait, what was I... right, the activities. Yeah, so I'm doing the backend, and I'm also mock-planning these huge interactive physical installations, and I'm trying to recruit other developers to help me out. I'm messaging them at all hours, like 3 or 4 AM, just trying to get them on board. I just have to, because this whole project... it just feels so much bigger and more important than my regular job now.
Have there been specific times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable — not just busy or productive, but different from your usual self in a more extreme way?

Yeah, I mean... high, energetic, sure. Most days lately I feel completely lit up, just unstoppable. It’s like the whole city of Glendale has finally caught up to the frequency I’m operating on, you know? The energy here has shifted. Glendale is actually such a weird place when you think about it. It’s got all these massive corporate buildings right next to these tiny little mom-and-pop bakeries. I went to this Armenian bakery the other day, got this huge box of pastries. The guy behind the counter was telling me about how his grandfather started the business in the 70s. The 70s must have been a wild time to start a business, before the internet, before you had to worry about SEO and digital marketing. I read an article about how SEO is basically ruining the internet because everything is just optimized for algorithms instead of human beings. 

But anyway, yeah, I feel amazing. Unstoppable. But then... people just get in my way. My wife, my coworkers... they keep trying to slow me down with all this talk about "process" and "doing things the right way." And honestly, I snap at them. I snap hard. It’s infuriating when you can see the whole picture and everyone else is just staring at their shoes. It’s like, why are we having a meeting about a meeting when I’ve already built the solution? My manager loves having meetings. He uses the phrase "circle back" at least five times a day. If I hear "circle back" one more time, I might actually lose my mind. So yeah, I guess I do get pretty irritable when people just can't keep up.
Have you had a period of time — at least a week or more — where you felt this way pretty much all day, every day, and not just in short bursts?

A week? Oh, way longer than a week. It’s been pretty much all day, every day for... I'd say about three months now. It all really locked in and started right after my platform got selected for the Glendale showcase. Which, by the way, the venue they’re using for that showcase is this incredible converted warehouse. Exposed brick, massive skylights... it’s gorgeous. 

My buddy actually used to live in a warehouse loft just like it back in Seattle, but he had to move out because the heating bill in the winter was just completely insane. Like, thousands of dollars just to keep the place above fifty degrees. Seattle gets so damp, too. I visited him once in November and it just rained for six days straight. I don't know how people deal with that constant gray and lack of sunlight, honestly. I need the sun, which is why I love it down here. I actually started growing tomatoes on my balcony because the light is so good, though the birds keep trying to get at them. I had to buy this reflective tape to scare them off... 

But wait, what were you asking? Right, the timeframe. Yeah, it hasn't been just short bursts at all. It's been a solid three months of this ever since I got that showcase selection email.
